steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Local government: county councils, district/borough councils, and parish/community councils provide local services. Responsibilities: education (schools), social services, housing, planning permission, waste collection, local roads, libraries, and leisure centres. Funded through council tax, business rates and government grants.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Councillors: elected by local residents to represent their ward. They make decisions about local services, set council tax rates, and approve planning applications. Councils are led by a council leader or directly elected mayor (e.g. Mayor of London, Metro Mayors in combined authorities).

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Devolved administrations: Scottish Parliament (129 MSPs), Welsh Senedd (60 MSs), Northern Ireland Assembly (90 MLAs) have powers over health, education, transport and environment in their nations. England does not have its own devolved parliament - English matters are decided at Westminster.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: How local decisions affect citizens: school closures, planning permission for new housing, waste collection schedules, library opening hours, parking restrictions, and social care provision are all decided locally. Citizens can influence decisions through: voting in local elections, attending council meetings, submitting planning objections, and contacting their councillor.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Local councils = ADMINISTRATIVE (manage services). Devolved bodies = LEGISLATIVE (can pass laws). Key difference. Local services: education, social care, housing, planning, waste. Funded by council tax + government grants. Local government is UNDER-FUNDED and UNDER-POWERED. Needs more resources to serve citizens effectively.
